title: Interstage warmup and burst profile suite for multi-GPU regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: build a reproducible test suite that captures interstage warmup behavior and burst (microburst) token emission profiles across tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) distributed model topologies. Rationale: recent regressions show identical steady-state tokens/sec but divergent p95 and cold-start tails when requests traverse different stage boundaries; we need deterministic detection and triage signals for these cases. Scope: multi-node TP/PP configs (TP=1-8, PP=1-8), heterogeneous GPU mixtures, with and without prefix/KV cache hits, and with variable batching/warmup sequences. Deliverables: 1) a parameterized workload harness that can replay recorded real-world burst traces, 2) a set of canonical warmup profiles (cold -> steady) and associated golden metrics, 3) regression detector with automatic baseline comparison and alerting, 4) dashboards and smoke test PR gates. Out of scope: full end-to-end client SDK changes; quantization experiments are separate.
success_criteria: 1) Harness can replay 95% of sampled production burst traces within 10% tokens/sec and within 15% p95 on same infra. 2) Regression detector raises an actionable alert when p95 increases by >=20% or tokens/sec drops by >=15% vs baseline across two consecutive runs. 3) Artifacts include reproducible scripts, one Grafana dashboard, and one smoke-test GitHub Action that runs on relevant PRs.
test_plan: Create synthetic burst generator that replays request timestamps and payload length distributions from anonymized production traces.
Run baseline matrix across TP in {1,2,4,8} x PP in {1,2,4} with and without KV cache warmed.
Measure tokens/sec (summary) and latency quantiles (p50, p90, p95, p99) per-stage and end-to-end.
Record cold-start profiles (first request after model restart) and warm-start profiles (after steady traffic resumes).
Introduce controlled perturbations (kernel change, small scheduling delay, serialized KV misses) to validate detector sensitivity and false positive rate.
Schedule nightly runs and compare to rolling 14-day baseline; store run artifacts in S3 for fast replay.
configurations: Hardware: a100-40g x4, a100-80g x8, mixed clusters (a100 + h100) - record GPU types per-run.
Model shapes: long-context (8k), medium (2k), short (512) - measure per-token cost and latency characteristics.
Batching: dynamic batching on and off; max_batch_size {1,8,32}; request-concurrency knobs.
KV cache: cold (cache empty), warmed prefix cache (simulated repeated prefixes), and full persistent cache scenarios.
Network: intra-node local vs cross-node (simulate interconnect contention by adding latency).
metrics: primary: tokens/sec (aggregate and per-stage), p95 end-to-end latency
secondary: p50/p90/p99, tail-degradation slope (p95->p99), throughput stability (stddev over 1m windows)
operational: GPU util, PCIe/NIC saturation, kernel invocation counts, batch formation latency
artifacts: Playbooks: runbook for triage when detector fires (links in Confluence).
pr_links: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1129 - enable stable node labels for bench clusters
dashboards: Alert: Prometheus rule: ENG-52709-p95-regression (fires on 20% sustained increase vs baseline)
CI smoke: GitHub Action job 'bench-smoke' that runs minimal TP/PP matrix on PRs touching runtime kernels

2026-03-09 - MG: Implemented regression detector prototype; compares run to baseline using bootstrapped CI and flags delta with context (per-stage breakdown). Need to tune thresholds to reduce FP on noisy configs.

notes: Trade-offs: tighter detector thresholds reduce missed regressions but increase noise; we'll use a two-tier approach (soft alert + hard alert after repeated runs). Focus initial effort on configs with highest customer impact (TP=2/4 x PP=1/2) and expand after stability. Operational cost: full sweep across all combos is expensive; use sampling and quick-fail smoke jobs for PRs.
